solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Shift to the left endorses first requirement of policy expert (9)

indicatorNotes.first requirement of: the first thing 'policy' requires is its opening letter

blocks.note: to back a plan is to endorse it
opening letter of policy
an ace is an expert

annotation.surface: A political story: a party lurching leftward while backing an expert's policy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shift to the left' reads as a political lurch, but it is the keyboard key that moves the cursor one place leftward.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by function: that keyboard key moves the cursor one position leftward, deleting as it goes.

entries.clue: British poet backed including British jazz (5)

indicatorNotes.backed: sent backwards, so POE becomes EOP
indicatorNotes.including: EOP takes the second B inside it

blocks.note: B = British
Edgar Allan POE, reversed
B = British, placed inside EOP to give EBOP

annotation.surface: A British poet who turns out to have been a jazz fan all along.
annotation.walkthrough: 'British' appears twice and gives B both times: once at the front, once tucked inside the reversed poet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: this is the fast, complex style that grew up in 1940s New York, one kind of jazz.

entries.clue: What’s out at the present time? (9,6)

annotation.definition: What’s out at the present time?

blocks.note: the surface hears 'out' as absent or unfashionable; the setter means in flower, as blooms come out
the surface hears 'now'; the setter means the season when presents are given

annotation.surface: A question about what is fashionable or available right now.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present time' looks like 'now', but it is the season of presents; 'out' means in bloom. The plant that flowers then is named after the season.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: this houseplant is named for flowering in late December, the time of presents.

entries.clue: What one seeks — forgiveness — a bishop withheld (8)

indicatorNotes.withheld: what is withheld is kept back, so A and B are taken out of the word

blocks.note: absolution is forgiveness of sins
A + B (bishop, as in chess notation), removed from the front

annotation.surface: A penitent seeking forgiveness, which a bishop refuses to give.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all about the church, which hides a definition that describes what every crossword solver is after.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose description: anyone facing a problem, or a crossword clue, is looking for the answer to it.

entries.clue: Broadcast cover of record that should take off (8)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for 'something that should take off', i.e. a plane

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a record's liner is its inner sleeve

annotation.surface: A DJ airing a record whose sleeve is expected to be a hit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests a record becoming a hit; here it is literal, an aircraft leaving the runway.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by function: a passenger plane is built to leave the ground, which is what 'take off' means literally.

entries.clue: Surround prince dropping in to opera company (6)

indicatorNotes.dropping in to: to drop in to a place is to go inside it, so HAL goes inside ENO

blocks.note: English National Opera, London's opera company
Prince Hal, Shakespeare's young Henry V, placed inside ENO

annotation.surface: A prince dropping by the opera and being mobbed.
annotation.walkthrough: ENO is the English National Opera; Prince Hal is the future Henry V in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary verb built from halo: to ring something with a circle of light, so to surround it.

entries.clue: Outstanding run eclipsed in sport (5)

indicatorNotes.eclipsed: something eclipsed is blotted out of sight, so the R disappears

blocks.note: rowing, the sport
R = run in cricket scoring, removed from ROWING

annotation.surface: A brilliant run in sport overshadowed by someone else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise for the run, but it means unpaid, as a debt is outstanding.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the accounting sense: an unpaid bill is both outstanding and yet to be settled.

entries.clue: Better than even extra offspring (4-2)

blocks.note: an odd one is spare, extra
a son is offspring

annotation.surface: A parent with an extra child who beats the rest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Even' teams up with 'odd' in the surface, but 'better than even' is betting talk: more likely than not.
annotation.definitionFit: A betting idiom: a favourite priced shorter than evens is more likely to win than lose.

entries.clue: Cruel ruler Ethelbert VII ran amok (4,3,8)

indicatorNotes.ran amok: to run amok is to go wild, and the letters go wild into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder; VII supplies V, I, I
also fodder, doing double duty with 'amok'

annotation.surface: A fictional seventh King Ethelbert rampaging as a cruel tyrant.
annotation.walkthrough: There was never an Ethelbert VII; the invented king exists to supply letters, including 'ran', which is fodder as well as part of the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Ivan IV of Russia earned his nickname through purges and violence.

entries.clue: Like old copper perhaps warning raw recruit (9)

blocks.note: old copper turns green with verdigris
a horn is sounded as a warning

annotation.surface: An old policeman warning a naive new recruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' wants to be a police officer giving a rookie a warning; it is the metal, which goes green with age.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean a newcomer with no experience, 'green' itself meaning untried.

entries.clue: Raffles, say, nearly all food sent back, right? (7)

indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly all of a word is all but its last letter
indicatorNotes.sent back: what is sent back returns the way it came, so AL + GRUB reads in reverse

blocks.note: ALL without its last letter
grub is food; ALGRUB reversed gives BURGLA
R = right

annotation.surface: Someone at a raffle sending almost all the food back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raffles' looks like prize draws; it is A. J. Raffles, E. W. Hornung's gentleman thief.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'say': Raffles is fiction's famous gentleman housebreaker.

entries.clue: Abnormal dry heat is cause to take in more water (7)

annotation.definition: cause to take in more water

indicatorNotes.Abnormal: something abnormal is not in its normal state, so the letters leave their normal order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Advice that a heatwave means you should drink more.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is sound health advice, so the whole clue reads as a single sentence and the anagram hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: A dictionary gloss: the verb comes from Greek hydor, water, and means to make something absorb it.

entries.clue: Advance column capturing island (5)

indicatorNotes.capturing: a captured thing is held inside, so POST holds I

blocks.note: a post is an upright column
I = island, placed inside POST

annotation.surface: A military column advancing and seizing an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Advance' and 'column' make a military picture, but advance here means put forward an idea.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of argument: both mean to put forward a proposition for discussion.

entries.clue: Terribly long title removed without asking (3-6)

indicatorNotes.Terribly: something done terribly is done badly, so the letters are badly arranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Someone stripped of a very long title without being consulted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Removed' looks like the instruction to take the title away, but it belongs to the definition: taken without asking, as stolen goods are.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose paraphrase: goods acquired dishonestly were taken from their owner without permission.

entries.clue: Promising person penning regular pieces for Proms? (8)

annotation.definition: Promising person penning regular pieces for Proms?

indicatorNotes.penning: to pen is to shut in, as sheep in a pen, so COMER shuts in POS
indicatorNotes.regular: regular pieces come at even intervals, so take every other letter

blocks.note: a comer is a promising newcomer
P, O, S: alternate letters of PROMS, placed inside COMER

annotation.surface: A rising talent writing works for the Proms concert season.
annotation.walkthrough: The Proms are the BBC's summer season of classical concerts in London. 'Person' does double duty: part of COMER and part of the definition, so the clue reads as a description of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by example: those who write music for concert seasons such as the Proms are what the word names.

entries.clue: Cooked corn, as it’s something for breakfast (9)

indicatorNotes.Cooked: cooked food is transformed from its raw state, so the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the rest of the fodder, S and all

annotation.surface: Cooked corn served up as a breakfast dish.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored: 'it’s' gives all three letters I, T, S, completing the nine.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the flaky French pastry is a standard breakfast item.

entries.clue: Note followed by second note (4)

indicatorNotes.followed by: what follows comes after, so MO is written after ME

blocks.note: me (or mi), the third note of the sol-fa scale
a mo is a moment, a second

annotation.surface: A musical phrase: one note then another.
annotation.walkthrough: Both ends of the clue say 'note'; the first is the musical note ME, the last is the written note that is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short written message, short for memorandum, is a note.

entries.clue: Song has the ability to amuse — not a Mozartian number (8)

indicatorNotes.not: 'not K' means without K, so the K is struck out of TICKLE

blocks.note: can = has the ability to
to tickle is to amuse
K = Köchel, the catalogue numbering Mozart's works, removed from TICKLE

annotation.surface: A song that can entertain, though it is not by Mozart.
annotation.walkthrough: Mozart's works are catalogued by Köchel number, as in K. 525, so a Mozartian number is K.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: a hymn from the Bible, such as the Magnificat, is a kind of song.

entries.clue: Dog turned up guarding unknown house (8)

indicatorNotes.guarding: a guard stands around what it protects, so FOUND goes around X and HO

blocks.note: something that turned up was found
x, the unknown in algebra, placed inside FOUND
HO = house, placed inside FOUND after X

annotation.surface: A stray dog appearing and guarding an empty house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' suggests a reversal; here it means appeared, so FOUND.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: a pack breed kept for hunting foxes is one kind of dog.

entries.clue: Dismiss author killing two leading characters (4)

indicatorNotes.killing two leading characters: to kill the leading characters is to cut off the first letters, here two of them

blocks.note: Marcel Proust, the French novelist, minus PR

annotation.surface: A writer killing off two main characters and being sacked for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leading characters' reads as protagonists; it means the first letters of the author's name.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to force someone out of a job or position.

entries.clue: Fabric to cover a horse from the time of Macbeth (8)

indicatorNotes.to cover: a cover lies over and around a thing, so JEAN wraps round A COB

blocks.note: jean is a heavy cotton fabric
placed inside JEAN
a cob is a sturdy horse, placed inside JEAN after A

annotation.surface: A cloth to throw over a horse, dating from Shakespeare's day.
annotation.walkthrough: Macbeth was written around 1606, in the reign of James I; Jacobus is Latin for James.
annotation.definitionFit: A period adjective: it names the reign of James I, during which Shakespeare wrote Macbeth.

entries.clue: Ratty and the rest in Toad Hall, yes initially (6)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so ETC goes inside the initials
indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so take the first letters of Toad, Hall and yes

blocks.note: initials of Toad Hall
etc. = et cetera, and the rest, placed inside TH
initial of yes

annotation.surface: Ratty and the other animals at Toad Hall, from The Wind in the Willows.
annotation.walkthrough: Ratty and Toad Hall come from The Wind in the Willows, which makes 'Ratty' look like a name; it is the definition, meaning irritable.
annotation.definitionFit: A British colloquial synonym: 'ratty' means bad-tempered, as does the answer.

entries.clue: A lot of animal homes around Australia (6)

indicatorNotes.around: one thing around another encircles it, so DENS encircles OZ

blocks.note: a den is a wild animal's lair
Oz = Australia, placed inside DENS

annotation.surface: Many dens of Australian wildlife.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' looks like 'many' qualifying the homes; 'A lot' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: multiples of twelve used loosely for a large number.

entries.clue: Dazed by drugs, leaving gaps between words? (6,3)

blocks.note: slang for stupefied, especially after taking drugs
a literal description of text set with blanks between the words

annotation.surface: A stoned writer whose typing drifts apart on the page.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, literal sense: words spaced out along a line.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the slang for being stupefied, and the literal sense of set apart with spaces.

entries.clue: Champion died for king (5)

blocks.note: a champion is a hero
D = died, as in genealogies

annotation.surface: A champion who gave his life for his king.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a knight dying for his monarch; the king is the biblical ruler of Judea.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ruler of Judea in the Nativity story held the title of king.

entries.clue: Live close to good source of water (5)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its end, so take the last letter of good

blocks.note: last letter of good
a well is a source of water

annotation.surface: Advice to live near a good water supply.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as 'near'; it means the last letter of the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain, slightly formal synonym: both mean to reside in a place.

entries.clue: Car meeting reported tailback could be prompter (7)

indicatorNotes.meeting: one thing meeting another joins up with it, so AUTO is placed next to the second piece
indicatorNotes.reported: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so QUEUE is spelt as CUE

blocks.note: auto = car
a tailback is a queue of traffic; it sounds like cue

annotation.surface: A car hitting a traffic jam, which may make the driver hurry along.
annotation.walkthrough: A tailback is a British queue of traffic. The answer is the British trade name for a teleprompter, the screen presenters read from.
annotation.definitionFit: A trade name used generically: the device feeds presenters their lines, prompting them.

entries.clue: Cold roll for pudding (7)

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
a roll of thunder is a rumble

annotation.surface: A cold bread roll served up as dessert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roll' tempts as a bread roll, fitting the food surface; it is the sound. Pudding is British for dessert.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: fruit baked under a buttery topping is a classic British dessert.

entries.clue: Appetising and pleasantly warm, nothing less (5)

indicatorNotes.less: 'less' means minus, so the O is subtracted from TOASTY

blocks.note: toasty = comfortably warm
O = nothing, removed from TOASTY

annotation.surface: Food described as appetising and warm, nothing more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nothing less' sounds like 'no less than'; it means O taken away.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe food with a pleasing flavour.

entries.clue: Veronica’s competently following career (9)

indicatorNotes.following: what follows comes after, so WELL is written after SPEED

blocks.note: to career is to rush along, to speed
well = competently

annotation.surface: A woman named Veronica doing well in her career.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Veronica' looks like a woman's name and 'career' like a job; Veronica is a plant genus, and career is the verb to rush.
annotation.definitionFit: A botanical name: Veronica is the Latin genus of these small blue-flowered wild plants.
